# Table — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a table when the data is genuinely tabular - several attributes per record, and the point is comparing them across rows. Give every column a header and keep the values in a column aligned, because the comparison is the whole reason the table exists. On a narrow screen a table that scrolls sideways is better than one that reflows into unrelated cards; a card list loses the comparison that made the table worth building. If each record stands alone and nothing is compared, that is a list, not a table.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use tonal head rows over data rows for scan order.
- Let wide tables scroll horizontally inside their wrapper.

**Don't**

- Don't center data text - start-align for scanning.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wrapper | resting | kern.table.wrapper | outline-variant border, 8px |

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| TableRoot | The `<table>` itself. The namespace `Table` also exposes all of the parts below. |
| TableHead | The `<thead>`. The header ROWS go here - see the warning below. |
| TableHeader | One `<th>`. A header CELL, not the header section. The names are one letter apart and they are not interchangeable. |
| TableBody | The `<tbody>`. |
| TableRow | One `<tr>`. |
| TableCell | One `<td>`. |
| TableCaption | The `<caption>`. Names the table for assistive tech - the only place a table gets a title it can announce. |

### FAQ

**Table or list?**

Tables for multi-column data; lists for single-column rows with actions.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a table when the content is genuinely tabular — the same few fields repeated per record — and the reader is comparing down a column. Columns are named and rows are keyed records of strings, so the data is a declaration and the table does the layout. Keep it to what fits: a compact screen compares two or three columns well and ten badly, and a row that needs to wrap into a paragraph wants a `ListItem` or a card instead. The table is a grid of text, so it is right for numbers and statuses and wrong for anything that needs its own controls per cell.
